title: Split match records in time
prompt: Implement chronological(rows,validation_start,test_start). Each row has numeric time. Return train (<validation_start), validation (>=validation_start and <test_start), test (>=test_start). Example times 10,20,30 with boundaries 20,30 give one per group.
tests:
rows=[{'time':10},{'time':20},{'time':29},{'time':30}]
g=chronological(rows,20,30)
assert g=={'train':[rows[0]],'validation':rows[1:3],'test':[rows[3]]}, 'Boundary records must appear in exactly one group'
assert chronological([],20,30)=={'train':[],'validation':[],'test':[]}, 'Keep the same structure for empty input'
hint: Write one list comprehension per interval.

title: Measure the population mix
prompt: Implement proportions(labels), returning a dictionary of observed category frequencies. Return {} for no labels. Example ['hog','hog','bait'] gives hog=2/3 and bait=1/3.
tests:

assert abs(p.get('hog',0)-2/3)<1e-10 and abs(p.get('bait',0)-1/3)<1e-10, 'Use the full population count'
assert proportions([])=={}, 'Empty data should not invent frequencies'

title: Adapt a copy, preserve the baseline
prompt: Implement fine_tune(base,x,y,steps=40): deep-copy base, use Adam at 0.05 and cross-entropy, update the copy for steps, return it. Keep base unchanged. This toy target uses two card classes; it is not a live result. Example zero-initialised Linear(2,2) should learn labels separating the two input coordinates.
starter:
import copy
import torch
from torch import nn

def fine_tune(base,x,y,steps=40):
    adapted=copy.deepcopy(base)
    # TODO: train only the copy
    return adapted
tests:
torch.set_num_threads(1)
base=nn.Linear(2,2)
with torch.no_grad():
    base.weight.zero_();base.bias.zero_()
x=torch.tensor([[1.,0.],[2.,0.],[0.,1.],[0.,2.]])
y=torch.tensor([0,0,1,1])
before=[p.detach().clone() for p in base.parameters()]
a=fine_tune(base,x,y)
assert a is not base, 'Return an independent model'
assert all(torch.equal(old,p) for old,p in zip(before,base.parameters())), 'Do not alter baseline parameters'
assert nn.functional.cross_entropy(a(x),y).item()<0.15, 'The copied model should learn the simple target labels'
z=fine_tune(base,x,y,steps=0)
assert all(torch.equal(p,q) for p,q in zip(base.parameters(),z.parameters())), 'Zero-step adaptation must preserve the copied values'
hint: Create Adam from adapted.parameters(), not base.parameters().
solution:
import copy
import torch
from torch import nn

def fine_tune(base,x,y,steps=40):
    adapted=copy.deepcopy(base)
    adapted.train()
    opt=torch.optim.Adam(adapted.parameters(),lr=0.05)
    for _ in range(steps):
        opt.zero_grad()
        loss=nn.functional.cross_entropy(adapted(x),y)
        loss.backward()
        opt.step()
    return adapted

title: Keep a forgetting guardrail
prompt: Implement acceptable(before,after,tolerance): dictionaries contain source and target losses. Return True only if target loss strictly decreases and source loss rises by no more than tolerance. Example before={source:1,target:2}, after={source:1.05,target:1.5}, tolerance=0.1 passes.
tests:
b={'source':1.,'target':2.}
assert acceptable(b,{'source':1.05,'target':1.5},0.1), 'A bounded source regression with target gain should pass'
assert not acceptable(b,{'source':1.3,'target':1.5},0.1), 'Do not hide excessive forgetting'
assert not acceptable(b,{'source':0.9,'target':2.},0.1), 'Target loss must strictly improve'
assert acceptable(b,{'source':0.9,'target':1.8},0), 'Improving both populations should pass'
hint: Use and to combine the two declared conditions.
